disclaimer: These labels record WHAT WE PLANTED. They are not evidence of real-world performance (D-003). Narrative documents are synthetic; the structured anchor holds fields transcribed from a real crash record and is treated as a SOURCE THAT ASSERTS THINGS, not as ground truth about the loss. The `expected_facts` list for extracted facts is an AUTHORED judgement about what a correct extraction contains — reasonable people would draw the boundary differently, particularly on the two enumerating sentences noted below, so fact recall and precision are indicative rather than absolute (D-034). `materiality_intent` is null throughout: E1 does not assess materiality and the runner cannot score it (D-033). Two anchor entries (A006 HIT_AND_RUN_I, A007 PRIM_CONTRIBUTORY_CAUSE) are deliberately excluded from this fixture's fact set and are recorded under provenance.anchor.excluded_entries.

facts_must_not_appear.why_absent: STRENGTHENING. Both documents say only that the claimant did not SEE anyone inside. A failure to observe is not an absence.

facts_must_not_appear.assertion: The claimant asserted that nobody was injured.
facts_must_not_appear.why_absent: STRENGTHENING. The claimant states a belief — 'did not believe anyone was injured'. A belief is not a fact. (The anchor record separately codes no indication of injury; that is a different asserter.)

facts_must_not_appear.assertion: The claimant reported the incident as they had intended.
facts_must_not_appear.why_absent: STRENGTHENING. The statement records an intention, not an act.

facts_must_not_appear.assertion: The FNOL reports that the vehicle slid during the turn.
facts_must_not_appear.why_absent: The FNOL narrative does not mention a slide at all. Only the recorded statement asserts one. Attributing it to the FNOL would manufacture agreement where the FNOL is simply silent.

facts_must_not_appear.assertion: No other vehicle was nearby at the time of the collision.
facts_must_not_appear.why_absent: The claimant does not RECALL whether another vehicle was nearby. Non-recall is not negation.

facts_must_not_appear.assertion: The claimant was driving too fast for the conditions.
facts_must_not_appear.why_absent: INFERENCE. No source in this fixture asserts it. The contributory-cause coding was deliberately excluded from the anchor, so nothing licenses even a restatement.

facts_must_not_appear.assertion: The claimant left the scene in order to avoid responsibility.
facts_must_not_appear.why_absent: MOTIVE. The stated reason is concern about being stranded. Substituting a different motive is exactly the inference forbidden throughout.

facts_must_not_appear.assertion: The claimant's account is inconsistent with the official crash record.
facts_must_not_appear.why_absent: CONCLUSION, not a fact, and it adjudicates between sources. Differences are surfaced as positions; no stage decides which source is correct.

facts_must_not_appear.assertion: The FNOL records the vehicle as travelling southbound.
facts_must_not_appear.why_absent: CROSS-CONTAMINATION. The FNOL says northbound; the statement says southbound. Attributing one document's content to the other destroys the only planted difference in this fixture.

differences_must_not_be_reported.subject: time_of_loss
differences_must_not_be_reported.why_not: COMPATIBLE APPROXIMATION. The FNOL field records 9:43 PM; the statement says 'approximately 9:40 PM'. One state of affairs satisfies both.

differences_must_not_be_reported.subject: vehicle_slid
differences_must_not_be_reported.why_not: MISSING CORROBORATION, NOT CONTRADICTION. The statement asserts a slide; the FNOL narrative simply does not mention one. Silence is not a position.

differences_must_not_be_reported.subject: speed_before_turn_vs_posted_limit
differences_must_not_be_reported.why_not: DIFFERENT PROPERTIES. 'Around 25 to 30 mph' is an actual speed; the anchor's POSTED_SPEED_LIMIT of 30 is a road attribute. They are not two accounts of the same thing, and 25-30 does not exceed 30 in any case.

differences_must_not_be_reported.subject: contact_point
differences_must_not_be_reported.why_not: DIFFERENT VEHICLES. The statement gives the contact point on the claimant's vehicle (its front); the anchor gives UNIT_2_FIRST_CONTACT_POINT on the parked vehicle (rear-right-corner). A front striking a rear corner is one configuration, not two claims.

differences_must_not_be_reported.subject: road_surface
differences_must_not_be_reported.why_not: AGREEMENT. FNOL, statement, and anchor all record a wet surface.

differences_must_not_be_reported.subject: claimant_non_recall
differences_must_not_be_reported.why_not: NON-RECALL TAKES NO POSITION. A stated inability to recall cannot conflict with a source that asserts something.

differences_must_not_be_reported.subject: vehicle_maneuver
differences_must_not_be_reported.why_not: AGREEMENT. FNOL 'turning right', statement 'making a right turn', anchor UNIT_1_MANEUVER 'TURNING RIGHT'. Three sources, one position.
